**Wire verb `library read` with `--paths-stdin`**: many inputs, one bridge process, one long table, per BULK.md.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wire `--paths-stdin` | `flag` | absent | — | — | Read MANY libraries: newline-delimited paths on stdin (blank lines ignored; a repeated path is a usage error). Exclusive with path; offset and limit are refused with it. |
| `threads` (wire `--threads`) | `int` | `1` | files | `>= 1, or -1 for one per core` | Libraries read at once. The output is byte-identical at any value (libraries are emitted in input order); 1 is the default because a library loaded whole is held in memory while its rows are written. |
| `on_error` (wire `--on-error`) | `string` | `fail` | — | `fail \| skip` | fail: the first unreadable library stops the batch with its usage or correctness error, the message starting 'Input &lt;i&gt; (&lt;path&gt;)'. skip: the failure goes in that input's files\[i\].error and the rest are read. skip with a single path is a usage error. |
| `out` (wire `--out`) | `path` | absent | — | `.tsv only, any case (PYB-1)` | Write the long table here, one library at a time in input order. A batch that stops on an error deletes its partial table. Must differ from every input. Must end in .tsv, any case (PYB-1); any other extension, or none, is a usage error before any input is read, and no extension is appended. |

# Returns

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_count` | `int` | files | never | Paths given. |
| `read_count` | `int` | files | never | Libraries read. |
| `failed_count` | `int` | files | never | Libraries not read; non-zero only under on-error skip. |
| `record_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors summed over the libraries read (BULK.md section 2). |
| `returned_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors returned in columns, summed over the libraries; 0 when written to out. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Rows in columns (one per fragment ion with fragments); 0 when written to out. |
| `on_error` | `string` | — | never | fail or skip, as requested. --threads is deliberately not echoed: the envelope is byte-identical at every thread count. |
| `fragments_included` | `bool` | — | never | Whether the rows are fragment ions. |
| `index_only_threshold` | `int` | bytes | never | The threshold applied to every library: the one given, or mzLib's default. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | source\_index, source\_path, then the single-library columns. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | yes: the table was written to out instead | One long table: rows grouped by input in input order, each library's rows in precursor\_index order, whatever --threads is. |
| `output` | `object` | — | yes: out was not given | {path, format: "tsv", row\_count}; written one library at a time. |
| `files` | `object[]` | — | never | One per input, in input order: the per-file block (path, file\_type, reader, format\_version, is\_compressed, is\_index\_only, target\_count, decoy\_count, proteoform\_count, min\_precursor\_mz, max\_precursor\_mz, record\_count, rows\_not\_read, retention\_time\_unit, caveats, column\_names, absent\_fields, failed\_fields, excluded\_fields, error). An unread input has error set and every fact it could not establish null or empty. |
